summary: Amita Chatterjee is an Indologist and philosopher who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University (attested 1999, 2009).
Amod Jayant Lele works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage (1913–2003) was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor of Indo-European Philology, General Linguistics, and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College (c. 1961–1978), and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (c. 1993–2003).
Amrith Krishna works in computational linguistics and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge and worked at Uniphore (attested 2023) and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist. She earned a PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald and held positions at Yale, CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her PhD from Columbia University and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2008.

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA from Wesleyan University and her MA and PhD from the University of Virginia, completing her doctorate under David Germano alongside numerous traditional teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a linguist and Japanologist. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and served as a professor at the University of Washington around 1995.

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated in Sri Lanka, including at S. Thomas' College and Royal College, Colombo, he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who received a doctorate from the University of Freiburg. He founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala, served as its Ācārya, and taught at Visva-Bharati and Patna universities.

Anagarika Munindra (1915–2003) was a Buddhist studies teacher who served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple (1953–1957). He was a disciple of Mahasi Sayadaw from 1957 to 1966 and also studied under Satya Narayan Goenka.
Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a teacher of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist who studied at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia. He held positions at Sweet Briar College and the University of Utah before becoming a professor at the University of Washington around 2002.

Anand Venkatkrishnan works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University in 2015 and is an Assistant Professor of the History of Religion in South Asia at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Ananda Guruge (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Ceylon and the University of London. He held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) studied at Wycliffe College and UCL. An Indologist, art historian, and philosopher, he directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon (c. 1903–1906) and served as a curator and fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) was an Indologist and historian. He was a professor and department head at Banaras Hindu University (c. 1930–1949), professor at Patna University (c. 1949–1957), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur (1916–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a professor at the Mithila Research Institute (c. 1960–1976) and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.

Anantanand Rambachan is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, and was a religion professor at St. Olaf College (c. 1985–2021).

Andrea Acri is an Indologist who completed his PhD at Leiden University (c. 2006–2011) under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen. In 2016, he became maître de conférences in tantric studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études.
